content:
Some time ago I made a PR to fix the precedence of by blocks. As a result, it will be possible to write my_lemma by my_tac rather than my_lemma <| by my_tac. This then matches the precedence of do. The discussion was at #lean4 > Unexpected parsing in `do`.

This requires 2 PRs for bootstrapping reasons, and the first one is lean#11495.

It's now been a while, so I wanted to ask if there are any obstacles to getting this merged?
I think Sebastian Graf is the relevant person, as they are working on the new do notation.
This doesn't directly have much to do with do notation - it is about by notation.
All of the discussion about motivation is about matching do, isn't it?

Well yes that is one way to motivate it. The original post that prompted me to look into this was simply someone who wrote foo by tac, expecting it to parse as foo <| by tac, but then getting some weird error.
My understanding is that "new do notation" is all about what goes after do, whereas this proposal is all about taking how the parsing before do works and doing the same thing for by.
Yes. That's all true. I'm just saying that Sebastian Graf might be the person who has the attention/context to review your PR.
